purpose.reader_question: Which operations exchange evidence and who decides what runs next in each workflow?
purpose.expected_reading: The panels distinguish a single call, a single-agent loop, a fixed pipeline, routing, parallel fan-out, evaluator feedback, runtime delegation, peer debate and one permitted repair.
purpose.claim: The arrangements differ in execution dependencies and in how they choose the next operation.
purpose.scope: Panels (a), (e) and (i) depict the three simulator execution structures. Other panels illustrate workflow arrangements.
permitted_inferences: Recover the operation dependencies, branch guards, message flow, control, and stopping rules shown.
prohibited_inferences: Runtime, per-attempt cost, failure rate or provider ranking from graph layout.
Relative performance, complete coverage, or empirical prevalence of the illustrative arrangements.

inputs.source_reference: The single-call, parallel and serial-repair branches of conditional_outcomes.
Section 2 and the figure caption define the topology, evidence flow and termination.

constructions.definition: Directed adjacency of named operations and boundaries, including guarded edges, shared-state exchange and bounded feedback.
constructions.method: The TikZ source places named nodes and draws edges between them. The positions encode adjacency only.

encodings.represents: Bold labels identify model calls. Unemphasised labels identify tools, rules, stored information or workflow boundaries.
